rulings.restated: Choose — [f1040 line Filing Status = 'single' → helper "Year parameter sli.base_other ($85,000)"] [f1040 line Filing Status = 'mfj' → helper "Year parameter sli.base_joint ($170,000)"] [f1040 line Filing Status = 'mfs' → helper "Year parameter sales.zero"] [f1040 line Filing Status = 'hoh' → helper "Year parameter sli.base_other ($85,000)"] [f1040 line Filing Status = 'qss' → helper "Year parameter sli.base_other ($85,000)"]
rulings.model: The IRS amounts are 'Single, head of household, or qualifying surviving spouse—$85,000' and 'Married filing jointly—$170,000', and the instructions say the deduction applies only if 'Your filing status is any status except married filing separately.' The restatement instead assigns $0 to married filing separately and goes on to compute a deduction, with no refusal for that status.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. A married filer filing separately cannot take the deduction, and the project gives zero for that status on Schedule 1 line 21 (sli.eligible tests the filing status and sli.deduction is zero), so the zero on line 5 for that status changes nothing; the line itself is shown only because the project figures every line.
